tyler: Quick ping — PR #17621 needs fast eyes for a small fallback fix blocking the canary merge tonight 21:00 UTC. Runtime + security approvals requested. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/17621

tyler: short context — we hit a rare routing fallback where client headers are missing and the runtime route lookup returns nil. That causes a panic on the hot path; this patch adds a defensive fallback and a unit test. Small change but merge blocked by runtime/security.

tyler: patch snippet:
```diff
- route := lookupRoute(req.Headers["x-rl-route"])
- // later: route.Name used directly
+ route := lookupRoute(req.Headers["x-rl-route"])
+ if route == nil {
+   // fallback to default runtime pool to avoid panic
+   route = defaultRoute()
+ }
```

kevin: on it, will run a quick local smoke and grepping for other callers. If this is truly only on the header path we should be fine. 15–20m. @lina FYI — canary owner tonight?

lina: i can take a look now. quick Q — can you add a unit test exercising a missing header + concurrent KV cache hit? keeps us from regressing.

tyler: yes, adding test now. will push in ~10m.

kevin: looked at the change locally — found an edge where lookupRoute can return a route with empty backend slice; that still panics later when we try to select backend[0]. suggest tightening check:
```go
if route == nil || len(route.Backends) == 0 {
  return defaultRoute()
}
```

tyler: good catch, updated to that. pushed another commit.

ci-bot: CI started for PR #17621 (linux/go tests, unit).

ci-bot: linux/go tests — failed — 2 tests failing (TestRouteFallback, TestKVCacheRace).

tyler: investigating failing tests, probably ordering flake in the race test. will add a small sleep and use sync.WaitGroup to stabilize.

lina: from a canary ops perspective, this looks low-risk once tests pass. please include a one-liner in the deployment notes: "prevents nil/empty-backend panic when route header missing" and add the canary toggle flag (already in the PR).

sara: quick sec — security check: any user-controlled header that could cause unexpected routing? if so, we should validate values length + characters to avoid header injection. Also confirm no new third-party deps.

tyler: security: header is internal envoy->platform only, not user-controlled. adding a guard on header length and validating allowed chars (alphanumeric + -_) in the helper. no new deps.

kevin: re-ran unit locally after the extra guard + wg fix — tests pass on my machine.

ci-bot: CI started for PR #17621 (retry).

ci-bot: linux/go tests — success. all checks passed.

lina: thanks everyone — i'm marking canary scheduled for 21:00 UTC. @kevin @sara please add your approval comments on the PR when you have a sec.

kevin: approved. :thumbsup:

sara: approved from security — no concerns. :lock:

tyler: thanks all, will merge at the window and monitor metrics. adding post-merge note to rollout doc. :rocket:
